Summary:
The source paper proposes “online distillation”: two neural networks are trained in parallel on disjoint data shards and encouraged to match each-other’s (possibly stale) predictions. This technique is claimed to (1) double effective training speed when additional pure SGD parallelism has saturated and (2) greatly improve reproducibility of the exact outputs a model produces. Experiments on the Criteo Ad, ImageNet and a 6 × 10¹¹-token language-model corpus support both claims.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]
The paper is short but clear; causal chains are explicit, enabling confident mapping. Minor inference was needed to relate “slower training” and “prediction irreproducibility” to AI-safety-relevant risks.

Inference strategy justification:
Where wording was implicit (e.g. “reproducibility” → reliability risk), moderate inference (edge confidence 2) linked to standard safety concerns. No speculative nodes were added.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All reasoning steps appearing in the abstract (risks, problem analyses, theoretical insights, design rationale, implementation details, empirical evidence, and the single concrete technique) are captured; both benefits (speed, reproducibility) share the same internal fabric, so all paths are interconnected.

Key limitations:
• Full paper may contain additional ablation details not present in the excerpt.
• Only one concrete intervention is described, so the fabric is comparatively small.
• Edge confidences for un-excerpted sections defaulted to “medium/strong” based on typical experimental rigor.
